svg.title: Sequence the Platform, or Sequence the Outcome?
svg.desc: A decision tree with three questions. The first asks whether anything has yet reached a real consumer. If not, the recommended path is one bounded data product delivered end to end; the alternative, building the platform and its frameworks first, is flagged as the warning branch because it produces no outcome to validate against. The second question asks whether a second workload is genuinely required by a consumer or is being added speculatively. The third asks whether a domain needs its own capacity, which turns on whether its workloads are actually contending for compute rather than on org-chart boundaries.

text.aria-label: Has anything reached a real consumer yet?

svg.text: Has anything reached a real consumer yet? — The root question. Everything else in the sequence depends on whether a real user is already being served.Fabric Data Architecture Strategy decision path — Is the workload analytical?, Can data remain in OneLake?, Choose governed Fabric workload boundary

text.aria-label: Is a second workload actually required?
text.title: Is a second workload actually required? — Second question: is the new workload pulled in by a consumer, or pushed in speculatively?
Platform-first delivery with no outcome — Frameworks, medallion layers, and governance models built before anything is consumed.
text.tspan: Finance delivers daily positions first, proves governance
and operations, then adds intraday risk on the same owned

svg.text: Deliver one bounded data product — One source, through OneLake, to one semantic model and one report that a named person actually uses.✓ Named data-product owner

text.aria-label: Does a domain need its own capacity?

svg.text: Does a domain need its own capacity? — Third question: separate capacity is a compute-contention and cost-boundary decision, not an org-chart one.✓ Capacity and recovery objective
In Atlas: select a choice → inspect evidence → drill into inputs, processing, outputs, example, controls, and risks.
